text: Developers can use individual Gazebo libraries such as gz-math, sdformat and gz-transport directly in their own C++ applications
quote: those who use individual Gazebo libraries (like `gz-math`, `sdformat`, or `gz-transport`) directly in their own C++ applications

text: Developers can write custom plugins that control robots, sensors and the environment
quote: Develop custom plugins for robot, sensor, and environment control.

text: Gazebo Sim can run headless, without the GUI, using the -s server-only flag
quote: Gazebo Sim can also be run headless, i.e. without the GUI, by using the `-s` (server only) flag.

text: The GUI can run on its own with the -g flag and connects to a running server instance
quote: the GUI can be run independently using the `-g` (gui only) flag. On start, the GUI will attempt to connect to a server instance.

text: A lightweight server-only package with no GUI or Qt dependencies is offered for headless and CI environments
quote: For headless and CI environments where the GUI is not needed, the `gz-sim10-server` package provides a lightweight alternative.

text: Users can copy SDF snippets from model pages on Gazebo Fuel and paste them into their own SDF files
quote: click on the `<>` icon in the model description page... to copy an SDF snippet into your clipboard. This snippet can be pasted directly into your custom SDF file.

text: A plugin-based interface provides several physics engines, including ODE, Bullet and DART
quote: A plugin based interface to physics engines, such as ODE, Bullet, and DART.

text: Users can create, inspect and interact with simulations through a plugin-based Qt graphical interface
quote: Create, introspect and interact with your simulations through plugin-based graphical interfaces powered by Gazebo GUI.

text: Extensive command-line tools are provided for inspecting and controlling simulations
quote: Extensive command line tools for increased simulation introspection and control.

text: Ready-made robot models (PR2, Pioneer2 DX, iRobot Create, TurtleBot) and physically accurate environment models are available through Gazebo Fuel
quote: Access numerous robots including PR2, Pioneer2 DX, iRobot Create, and TurtleBot, and construct environments using other physically accurate models available through Gazebo Fuel

text: Simulations can run on remote servers and be accessed through socket-based message passing via Gazebo Transport
quote: Run simulation on remote servers and interface to Gazebo Sim through socket-based message passing using Gazebo Transport.

text: Simulated sensor data, optionally with noise, from lidar, 2D/3D cameras, depth, contact, force-torque, IMU, GPS and other sensors
quote: Generate sensor data, optionally with noise, from laser range finders, 2D/3D cameras, Kinect style sensors, contact sensors, force-torque, IMU, GPS, and more

text: Realistic rendering with high-quality lighting, shadows and textures using engines such as OGRE v2
quote: it's possible to use rendering engines such as OGRE v2 for realistic rendering of environments with high-quality lighting, shadows, and textures.

text: Asynchronous publish/subscribe messaging with service calls and discovery
quote: Asynchronous message publication and subscription is provided along with service calls and discovery.

text: A C++ client library and command-line tools for interacting with Gazebo Fuel servers
quote: A C++ client library and command line tools for interacting with Gazebo Fuel servers

text: A single command launches both the sim server and GUI with an example world
quote: This command will launch both the Sim server and Sim GUI with a world that contains six simple shapes.

text: Example SDF worlds ship with Gazebo Sim and can be freely copied and modified
quote: Gazebo Sim ships with a number of example SDF worlds that you can freely copy and modify.

text: The -v 4 flag prints error, warning, info and debug messages to the console
quote: Add the `-v 4` command line argument to generate error, warning, informational, and debugging messages on the console.

text: A single command installs the matching Gazebo and ros_gz versions for your ROS installation on Linux
quote: The following command will install the correct version of Gazebo and `ros_gz` for your ROS installation on a Linux system.

text: Documentation and a compatibility table cover which ROS and Gazebo versions work together
quote: This table includes all currently supported versions of ROS and Gazebo.

text: From ROS 2 Jazzy onward, Gazebo is available from the ROS package repository as vendor packages
quote: As of ROS 2 Jazzy, Gazebo is available from the ROS package repository via vendor packages.

text: Gazebo Harmonic can be used with ROS 2 Humble through unofficial binary packages from packages.osrfoundation.org
quote: Gazebo Harmonic can be used with ROS 2 Humble and non ROS official binary packages hosted in `packages.osrfoundation.org`.

text: The gz-jetty metapackage installs all Gazebo libraries at once
quote: To install all of them, the metapackage `gz-jetty` can be installed.

text: Binary installs can be uninstalled or swapped for a source-based install
quote: If you need to uninstall Gazebo or switch to a source-based install once you have already installed the library from binaries

text: A configuration script can specify which programs and plugins to run
quote: A configuration script can be used to specify which programs and plugins to run.

text: A small, fast, self-contained math library suited to robot applications
quote: A small, fast, and high performance math library. This library is a self-contained set of classes and functions suitable for robot applications.

text: Users can run simulations with standard tools, edit SDFormat files, use existing plugins and interact with running simulations from outside
quote: Users: For those who primarily run Gazebo using standard tools (like gz sim), edit SDFormat files, use existing plugins, and interact with running simulations from the outside
